title: Nvidia introduces 64GB DGX Spark to throw local AI fans a lifeline amid the RAMpocalypse — new GB10 config starts at $4999 for those who can work with less
key_facts: Nvidia is adding a 64GB version of its DGX Spark small AI computer, aimed at people who do not need the 128GB model.
64GB GB10 systems from Acer, Asus, Dell, Gigabyte, HP and MSI are slated to start at $4,999 when they launch on 23 Oct 2026.
Tom's Hardware says the price may not stay there for long, because memory and storage prices keep shifting.
Where 128GB systems can be found in stock, Tom's Hardware says they cost roughly $7,000 to $9,000 now.
The 64GB model keeps the same ConnectX 7 networking chip, the same 20-core Arm processor and the same 273 GB/s memory bandwidth as the 128GB model.
Nvidia is also adding a Sync Cluster Assistant to link several Sparks together, and a Model Launcher in Sync that downloads and starts models and connects them to the OpenCode coding agent.
The 128GB Spark stays on sale for larger models, clusters and fine-tuning.
quote_evidence: The company is introducing a 64GB version of the Spark that's meant to be more affordable to local AI trailblazers who just don't need 128GB of RAM.
64GB GB10 systems from Acer, Asus, Dell, Gigabyte, HP, and MSI are slated to start at $4999 when they launch on October 23.
Given the ever-shifting prices of memory and storage right now, they might not stay there for long.
why_it_matters_hint: A lower-memory model gives people who run AI models on their own desk a cheaper entry point while memory prices are high.
